sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Hezbollah is a Lebanese Shia Islamist political party with an active paramilitary wing.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Its military and security activities have been prohibited by the Lebanese government since March 2026, amid the 2026 Lebanon war.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Hezbollah's paramilitary wing is the Jihad Council, and its political wing is the Loyalty to the Resistance Bloc party in the Lebanese Parliament.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Its armed strength was assessed to be equivalent to that of a medium-sized army in 2016.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Hezbollah was founded in 1982 by Lebanese Shiite clerics in close cooperation with Iran.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: It emerged in the context of the Lebanese civil war, the collapse of central authority, Iran's strategic interests in Lebanon, and the Israeli invasion of Lebanon.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The movement's formation was shaped by the Iranian Revolution of 1979 and Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini's model of Islamic governance.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Hezbollah subsequently established strong ties with Iran as part of the "Axis of Resistance".

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The group was initially supported by 1,500 Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) instructors, who helped unify various Lebanese Shia factions under Hezbollah's leadership.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Hezbollah's 1985 manifesto outlined its key objectives, which include expelling Western influence from the region, destroying Israel, pledging allegiance to Iran's supreme leader, and establishing an Islamic government influenced by Iran's political ideology.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: However, the manifesto also emphasised Lebanese self-determination.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, Hezbollah fought against Israeli forces and the South Lebanon Army (SLA), eventually leading to Israel's withdrawal from southern Lebanon in 2000.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Hezbollah also played a prominent role in the 2006 Lebanon War and later became involved in the Syrian civil war, where it fought alongside the government of Bashar al-Assad against the ultimately victorious Syrian opposition forces.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: In 2009, Hezbollah issued a new manifesto to oppose political sectarianism, broaden its appeal to non-Islamic movements, and promote a national unity government.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The updated manifesto retained the same basic approach to foreign policy, emphasising what it characterizes as 'hegemonic strategies' of the U.S. and portraying Israel as its forward base for dominating the region.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Since the 1990s, Hezbollah has grown into a significant political force in Lebanon.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The group operates a vast social services network, including schools and hospitals, and runs a satellite TV station, Al-Manar.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Politically, Hezbollah's Loyalty to the Resistance Bloc holds 15 seats in the Lebanese Parliament, making it a powerful player in Lebanon's government.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: However, the group's influence has led to growing domestic criticism.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Following the 2020 Beirut port explosion, Hezbollah was accused of obstructing efforts to hold those responsible accountable, contributing to a decline in public trust.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: A 2024 Arab Barometer survey found that 55% of Lebanese have "no trust at all" in Hezbollah, although it remains popular among the Shia population.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Despite calls for disarmament under United Nations Security Council resolutions, Hezbollah has expanded its military capabilities.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: In 2013, its armed wing is considered stronger than the Lebanese Armed Forces, making it one of the most powerful non-state actors in the world.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah declared in 2021 that the group had 100,000 fighters.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Hezbollah has been involved in several high-profile attacks; it is believed to be responsible for the bombing of the US embassy and the US and French barracks bombings in Beirut in 1983, the assassination of Rafic Hariri in 2005, as well as later attacks, including bombings and hijackings.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: While Hezbollah has been regarded as a resistance movement by some scholars, the entire organisation, or its military wing alone, has been designated as a terrorist group by at least 28 countries as of April 2026, including most Western countries.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Since October 2023, Hezbollah has been at war with Israel.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: During this war, Nasrallah was assassinated after 32 years of leading the group, along with other key members of Hezbollah leadership.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The conflict has led to the 2024 Lebanon War, which saw Southern Lebanon invaded by Israel, followed by a ceasefire.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: On 7 August 2025, in a government meeting specifically addressing the disarmament of Hezbollah, the majority of the government voted to approve the decision.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The Lebanese Army was tasked to create a plan ensuring that only the state has control over weapons in Lebanon.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The decision is based on a US plan to disarm Hezbollah.

sentences.section: (lead)

sentences.section: (lead)

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: In 1982, Hezbollah was conceived by Lebanese clerics and funded by Iran primarily to fight the Israeli invasion of Lebanon.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: The 1982 and the 1978 Israeli invasions had created a humanitarian crisis in Lebanon; many villages in the south had been destroyed and large numbers of Shias had been displaced from their homes.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: In addition, the Shia had long been underrepresented in Lebanese politics.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Both these factors fostered resentment among the local Shia population, making them a fertile ground for recruitment.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Hezbollah was set up by local Shia committees under the leadership of Iran's first supreme leader, Ruhollah Khomeini.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Hezbollah's forces were trained and organised by a contingent of 1,500 Iranian Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) that arrived from Iran with permission from the Syrian government occupying Lebanon's eastern highlands, which allowed the IRGC's transit to a base in the Beqaa Valley.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Scholars differ as to when Hezbollah came to be a distinct entity.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Various sources list the official formation of the group as early as 1982, whereas Diaz and Newman maintain that Hezbollah remained an amalgamation of various violent Shia extremists until as late as 1985.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Another version states that it was formed by supporters of Sheikh Ragheb Harb, a leader of the southern Shia resistance killed by Israel in 1984.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Regardless of when the name came into official use, a number of Shia groups were slowly assimilated into the organisation, such as Islamic Jihad, Organisation of the Oppressed on Earth and the Revolutionary Justice Organisation.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: These designations are considered to be synonymous with Hezbollah by the US, Israel, and Canada.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: According to Robert Fisk and Israeli General Shimon Shapira, the date of 8 June 1982, two days after the Israeli invasion of Lebanon, when 50 Shiite militants ambushed an Israel Defence Forces armoured convoy in Khalde south of Beirut, is considered by Hezbollah as the founding myth of their military wing.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: It was in this battle, delaying the Israeli advance to Beirut for six days, that the future Hezbollah military chief Mustafa Badreddine made his name as a serious commander.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: According to Shapira, the lightly armed Shia fighters managed to capture an Israeli armoured vehicle on that day and paraded it in the Revolutionary Guards' forward operating base in Baalbek, Eastern Lebanon.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Fisk writes:

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Down at Khalde, a remarkable phenomenon had taken shape.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: The Shia militiamen were running on foot into the Israeli gunfire to launch grenades at the Israeli armour, actually moving to within 20 feet of the tanks to open fire at them.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Some of the Shia fighters had torn off pieces of their shirts and wrapped them around their heads as bands of martyrdom as the Iranian revolutionary guards had begun doing a year before when they staged their first mass attacks against the Iraqis in the Gulf War a thousand miles to the east.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: When they set fire to one Israeli armoured vehicle, the gunmen were emboldened to advance further.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: None of us, I think, realised the critical importance of the events of Khalde that night.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: The Lebanese Shia were learning the principles of martyrdom and putting them into practice.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: Never before had we seen these men wear headbands like this; we thought it was another militia affectation but it was not.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: It was the beginning of a legend which also contained a strong element of truth.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: The Shia were now the Lebanese resistance, nationalist no doubt but also inspired by their religion.

sentences.section: History
sentences.text: The party of God – in Arabic, the Hezbollah – were on the beaches of Khalde that night.
Hezbollah emerged in South Lebanon during a consolidation of Shia militias as a rival to the older Amal Movement.
Hezbollah played a significant role in the Lebanese civil war, opposing US forces in 1982–83 and opposing Amal and Syria during the 1985–88 War of the Camps.
However, Hezbollah's early primary focus was ending Israel's occupation of southern Lebanon following Israel's 1982 invasion and siege of Beirut.
Amal, the main Lebanese Shia political group, initiated guerrilla warfare.
In 2006, former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak stated, "When we entered Lebanon ... there was no Hezbollah.
We were accepted with perfumed rice and flowers by the Shia in the south.
It was our presence there that created Hezbollah."
Hezbollah waged an asymmetric war using suicide attacks against the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) and Israeli targets outside of Lebanon.

Hezbollah is reputed to have been among the first Islamic resistance groups in the Middle East to use the tactics of suicide bombing, assassination, and capturing foreign soldiers, as well as murders and hijackings.
Hezbollah also employed more conventional military tactics and weaponry, notably Katyusha rockets and other missiles.

At the end of the Lebanese Civil War in 1990, despite the Taif Agreement asking for the "disbanding of all Lebanese and non-Lebanese militias", Syria, which controlled Lebanon at that time, allowed Hezbollah to maintain their arsenal and control Shia areas along the border with Israel.

sentences.section: After 1990
sentences.text: In the 1990s, Hezbollah transformed from a revolutionary group into a political one, in a process which has been described as the "Lebanonisation" of Hezbollah.

sentences.section: After 1990
sentences.text: Unlike its uncompromising revolutionary stance in the 1980s, Hezbollah conveyed a lenient stance towards the Lebanese state.

sentences.section: After 1990
sentences.text: In 1992, Hezbollah decided to participate in elections, and Ali Khamenei, supreme leader of Iran, endorsed it.

sentences.section: After 1990
sentences.text: Former Hezbollah secretary general, Subhi al-Tufayli, contested this decision, which led to a schism in Hezbollah.

sentences.section: After 1990
sentences.text: Hezbollah won all twelve seats which were on its electoral list.

sentences.section: After 1990
sentences.text: At the end of that year, Hezbollah began to engage in dialogue with Lebanese Christians.

sentences.section: After 1990
sentences.text: Hezbollah regards cultural, political, and religious freedoms in Lebanon as sanctified, although it does not extend these values to groups who have relations with Israel.

sentences.section: After 1990
sentences.text: In 1997, Hezbollah formed the multi-confessional Lebanese Brigades to Fight the Israeli Occupation in an attempt to revive national and secular resistance against Israel, thereby marking the "Lebanonisation" of resistance.

sentences.section: Islamic Jihad Organisation (IJO)
sentences.text: Whether the Islamic Jihad Organisation (IJO) was a nom de guerre used by Hezbollah or a separate organisation, is disputed.

sentences.section: Islamic Jihad Organisation (IJO)
sentences.text: According to certain sources, IJO was identified as merely a "telephone organisation", and whose name was "used by those involved to disguise their true identity".

sentences.section: Islamic Jihad Organisation (IJO)
sentences.text: Hezbollah reportedly also used another name, "Islamic Resistance" (al-Muqawama al-Islamiyya), for attacks against Israel.

sentences.section: Islamic Jihad Organisation (IJO)
sentences.text: A 2003 US court decision found IJO was the name used by Hezbollah for its attacks in Lebanon, parts of the Middle East, and Europe.

sentences.section: Islamic Jihad Organisation (IJO)
sentences.text: The US, Israel, and Canada consider the names "Islamic Jihad Organisation", "Organisation of the Oppressed on Earth" and the "Revolutionary Justice Organisation" to be synonymous with Hezbollah.

sentences.section: Axis of Resistance
sentences.text: The group receives substantial financial and military backing from Iran, by smuggling and other measures, positioning itself as the leading member of the "Axis of Resistance", an alliance in opposition to Israel and Western influence in the Middle East.

sentences.section: Axis of Resistance
sentences.text: In mid-September 2024, Israel detonated thousands of communication devices distributed to Hezbollah operatives, including pagers and walkie-talkies, which exploded simultaneously across Lebanon.

sentences.section: Axis of Resistance
sentences.text: The attacks exposed deep vulnerabilities in Hezbollah networks.

sentences.section: Axis of Resistance
sentences.text: Following the outcome of the 2024 Lebanon War, the 2024 Syrian opposition offensives, the downfall of the Assad regime and the weakening of the Axis of Resistance, Hezbollah has withdrawn the majority of its military infrastructure from southern Lebanon, transferring control to the Lebanese army.

sentences.section: Axis of Resistance
sentences.text: This move aligns with the November 2024 U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement, which mandates Hezbollah's repositioning north of the Litani River and the deployment of approximately 5,000 Lebanese troops to the south.

sentences.section: Axis of Resistance
sentences.text: The withdrawal aims to reduce tensions along the Israel-Lebanon border and facilitate the return of displaced civilians.

sentences.section: Axis of Resistance
sentences.text: While Hezbollah has removed heavy weaponry, some fighters from southern villages remain with light arms.

sentences.section: Axis of Resistance
sentences.text: The situation remains delicate, with ongoing monitoring by international observers to ensure compliance with the ceasefire terms.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: As part of the ceasefire agreement that ended the 2024 Israeli invasion of Lebanon, and with mounting pressure from the US, the Lebanese Armed Forces have undertaken efforts to disarm Hezbollah, including in its traditional strongholds in southern Lebanon, with the aid of Israeli intelligence.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: In May 2025, the Lebanese government had announced that the army had largely achieved its aim.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: On 5 August 2025, the Lebanese government declared that a plan would be scheduled for the disarmament of the militias after a six-hour cabinet meeting with president Joseph Aoun.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: According to the Lebanese government, Hezbollah has handed over control of several critical facilities.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: Information minister Paul Morcos stated that a deadline of the end of 2025 was set for disarmament.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem condemned the disarmament proposal, stating: "The resistance is fine, strong and ready to fight for Lebanon's sovereignty and independence...

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: Hezbollah made heavy sacrifices to defend Lebanon against the Israeli aggression."

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: He warned that Hezbollah was prepared to renew attacks on Israel and said all of Lebanon would unite to counter Israel.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: On 22 August, Qassem threatened a civil war if the disarmament proposal went forward, which prime minister Nawaf Salam condemned as "completely unacceptable".

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: On 7 August, the cabinet of ministers approved the objective of the disarmament proposal, ensuring that arms in Lebanon are only possessed by the state.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: Hezbollah and Amal Movement-affiliated ministers walked out of the cabinet meeting in protest, and thousands of Hezbollah supporters rallied against the approval in the southern suburbs of Beirut.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: On 5 September, the Lebanese army presented the disarmament plan to the government.

sentences.section: Disarmament
sentences.text: On 5 September 2025, General Rodolphe Haykal presented to the Lebanese cabinet the Homeland Shield Plan, its roadmap for the disarmament of all militias in Lebanon, specifically Hezbollah.

On 2 March 2026, Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam condemned Hezbollah's rocket and drone strikes from southern Lebanon, calling them irresponsible acts outside the authority of the Lebanese state that endanger national security.
While he emphasised that all military action must fall under the government's control, he has not formally declared Hezbollah outlawed, focusing instead on preventing unauthorised armed operations.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: The ideology of Hezbollah has been summarised as Shia Islamist radicalism; Hezbollah follows the Islamic Shia theology developed by Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Hezbollah was largely formed with the aid of the Khomeini's followers in the early 1980s in order to spread Islamic revolution and follows a distinct version of Islamic Shia ideology (Wilayat al-faqih or Guardianship of the Islamic Jurists) developed by Khomeini, who was the leader of the "Islamic Revolution" in Iran.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Although Hezbollah originally aimed to transform Lebanon into an Islamic republic, this goal has been abandoned in favour of a more inclusive approach.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Early on, Hezbollah was influenced by ideas from prominent Sunni Islamists.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Hezbollah's own rhetoric was Islamist in general, rather than Shia in particular.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Hezbollah's position on the Sunni-Shia divide was that instead of dwelling on theological differences, Sunnis and Shias ought to cooperate with one another to oppose the Israeli occupation of Arab lands.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: To maintain a sense of Muslim unity, Hezbollah avoided direct criticism of Saudi Arabia; even during the 2007 Lebanon's conflict with the Salafis, Al-Manar TV's employees had instructions "not to talk badly about Saudi Arabia".

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: This changed, however, after the beginning of the Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Hezbollah has been described as socially conservative.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: It is against homosexuality and LGBT rights.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: In 2023, Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah called for gay people to be killed and said that the LGBT community was a "threat to society".

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: The organisation also encourages women to wear traditional Islamic veils, especially the full-body chador.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Some scholars consider Hezbollah to have become a left-wing political movement; including political scientists Anisseh van Engeland and Rachael Rudolph, Imad Salamey, Amal Saad-Ghorayeb, and As'ad Abu Khalil.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Salamey described Hezbollah as "a revolutionary proletarian party with an Islamic manifesto".

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Feminist Judith Butler controversially called Hezbollah part of the "global left" because they define themselves as anti-imperialist.

sentences.section: Ideology
sentences.text: Communist writer Nahla Chahal wrote that Hezhollah "is a movement of the Theology of Liberation".

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: On 16 February 1985, Sheik Ibrahim al-Amin issued Hezbollah's manifesto.

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: The ideology presented in it was described as radical.

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: Its first objective was to fight against what Hezbollah described as US and Israeli imperialism, including the Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon and other territories.

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: The second objective was to gather all Muslims into an "ummah", under which Lebanon would further the aims of the 1979 Revolution of Iran.

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: It also declared it would protect all Lebanese communities, excluding those that collaborated with Israel, and support all national movements—both Muslim and non-Muslim—throughout the world.

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: The manifesto by Hezbollah rejects the existence of the state of Israel, calling for its destruction.

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: Translated excerpts from Hezbollah's original 1985 manifesto read:

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: We are the sons of the umma (Muslim community) ...

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: ... We are an ummah linked to the Muslims of the whole world by the solid doctrinal and religious connection of Islam, whose message God wanted to be fulfilled by the Seal of the Prophets, i.e., Prophet Muhammad. ...

sentences.section: 1985 manifesto
sentences.text: As for our culture, it is based on the Holy Quran, the Sunna and the legal rulings of the faqih who is our source of imitation ...

sentences.section: 2009 manifesto
sentences.text: On 30 November 2009, secretary-general Hassan Nasrallah presented a new manifesto at Hezbollah's 7th political conference.

sentences.section: 2009 manifesto
sentences.text: Besides its introduction, this 32-page document has three chapters on U.S. hegemonic strategies and the impact of globalization; Hezbollah's approach to Lebanon; and Palestinian resistance to Israel.

sentences.section: 2009 manifesto
sentences.text: While self-described as a "rebirth" document, the manifesto conveys the same basic approach to foreign policy as in the past, according to scholar Benedetta Berti, though it is more "politically savvy" and appeals to non-Islamic movements.

sentences.section: 2009 manifesto
sentences.text: Still, the manifesto offers new support for Lebanese political institutions, through which it had been making inroads.

sentences.section: 2009 manifesto
sentences.text: Notably, it says that it opposes political "sectarianism", idealises a national unity government, and treats the Lebanese army less as an enemy and more as a subordinate military arm.

sentences.section: Attitudes, statements, and actions concerning Israel and Zionism
sentences.text: From the inception of Hezbollah to the present, the elimination of the State of Israel has been one of Hezbollah's primary goals.

sentences.section: Attitudes, statements, and actions concerning Israel and Zionism
sentences.text: Some translations of Hezbollah's 1985 Arabic-language manifesto state that "our struggle will end only when this entity [Israel] is obliterated".

sentences.section: Attitudes, statements, and actions concerning Israel and Zionism
sentences.text: According to Hezbollah's Deputy-General, Naim Qassem, the struggle against Israel is a core belief of Hezbollah and the central rationale of Hezbollah's existence.

sentences.section: Attitudes, statements, and actions concerning Israel and Zionism
sentences.text: Hezbollah says that its continued hostilities against Israel are justified as reciprocal to Israeli operations against Lebanon and as retaliation for what they claim is Israel's occupation of Lebanese territory.

sentences.section: Attitudes, statements, and actions concerning Israel and Zionism
sentences.text: Israel withdrew from Lebanon in 2000, and their withdrawal was verified by the United Nations as being in accordance with resolution 425 of 19 March 1978; however, Lebanon considers the Shebaa farms—a piece of land captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 war and considered by the UN to be Syrian territory occupied by Israel—to be Lebanese territory.

sentences.text: Finally, Hezbollah considers Israel to be an illegitimate state.
